newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-LAKERS LOSE FORWARD HORRY WITH SPRAINED KNEE.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-LAKERS LOSE FORWARD HORRY WITH SPRAINED KNEE.

text.p: Los Angeles Lakers forward Robert Horry will be sidelined for at least six weeks after an MRI exam revealed a sprained left knee ligament, the team announced Monday.
Horry, acquired in January from the Phoenix Suns, went down after drawing a foul from Seattle forward Terry Cummings in the fourth quarter the Lakers' loss on Sunday.
An MRI exam Monday revealed an isolated sprain of the medial collateral ligament, a team spokesman said.
Horry is the second Lakers starter in a week to go down for an extended period with a knee injury.
All-Star centre Shaquille O'Neal will be out eight to 10 weeks after suffering a hyperextended left knee, fractured bone and partial tear of the lateral collateral ligament.
The Lakers are currently 37-14, a half game ahead of the Utah Jazz for the best record in the Western Conference and 1-1/2 games ahead of Seattle for the Pacific Division lead.
Horry was traded to the Lakers in a multi-player deal days after an altercation on the Phoenix bench in which he threw a towel in the face of Suns coach Danny Ainge.
The 26-year-old Horry, who helped the Houston Rockets to NBA titles in 1994 and 1995, had been struggling this season, averaging career lows of 7.6 points and 4.2 rebounds per game.
